verdict: W75's ceiling attribution was invalid. Corrected instrument landed; the 111% itself is still not reproduced.

whatW75GotWrong.claim: W75 named 'raf :: m20Q6InertableScheduledCallback << m20Q6TrackScheduler' as the dominant CPU consumer at 55%, plus 19% and 5% on the same name.
whatW75GotWrong.problem: m20Q6InertableScheduledCallback is not product code. It is the M20-Q6 lifecycle wrapper installed around EVERY setTimeout/rAF callback so they can be made inert on teardown (replay-system.js m20Q6TrackScheduler). The profiler's stack filter did not skip those frames, so ~79% of busy time collapsed into a single bucket named after the instrumentation shim.
whatW75GotWrong.consequence: That evidence would have sent A to optimise a wrapper. It names no product call site.
whatW75GotWrong.fix: po-cpu-ab-benchmark.mjs stack filter now skips m20Q6InertableScheduledCallback / m20Q6TrackScheduler / m20Q6CapturedScheduler / m20Q6CaptureEffects so the real scheduling call site surfaces.

secondErrorInThePremise.issue: W75 also reported canvasPaintCalls=10512 over 8.1s and I was about to read that as ~21 repaints per frame.
secondErrorInThePremise.correction: The probe wraps fillRect/fill/stroke/drawImage individually, so one candlestick repaint of ~300-600 candles issues hundreds of calls. 1300 calls/s is a handful of repaints per second, not paint amplification. Total canvasPaintMs was 9.2ms in 8.1s — drawing is negligible on that surface.

whyTheHarnessCannotSeeTheCeiling.measured: workRatio 0.069 — the hermetic single-chart harness at 60x spends ~7% of one core in callbacks, with 93% of the timeline in 'system' (idle wait).
whyTheHarnessCannotSeeTheCeiling.structuralReason: The PO's figure is ~111% of a core. Anything above 100% cannot be main-thread JavaScript by definition. A setTimeout/rAF callback probe only ever samples CrRendererMain, so it can never account for the excess — that work is on compositor, raster, GPU or worker threads.
whyTheHarnessCannotSeeTheCeiling.conclusion: W75 did not characterise the ceiling; it characterised a 7% main-thread budget on a surface that is not pegged. Marking P3 characterised was wrong.

newInstrument.name: CPU-THREAD-CENSUS-V1
newInstrument.what: Sums Chrome trace event durations per thread (pid/tid -> thread_name), so the total is allowed to exceed one core — the shape that has to be reproduced.
newInstrument.correctnessGuard: Per-thread busy time is the UNION of event intervals, not the sum: nested trace events (a parent RunTask containing FunctionCall children) would otherwise double count and manufacture a >100% reading out of an idle browser. Unit tests cover nesting, partial overlap, instant/async events, and the empty-trace case (which returns NO-DATA rather than a 0% pass).
newInstrument.assessment: assessCpuCeiling() reports BELOW-CLAIM rather than treating a low main-thread reading as a refutation of the PO.
